No Rape Kits

By: Sasha OLD | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Although our FCS units have some of the most exemplary officers in the country, there is little they can do when they don't have the basics - like rape kits.

Unique Selling Point:
As of February this year we were leaked the rape kit stats from the various provinces, and it's appalling. Only 19.8% of SA police stations had at least 1 rape kit for adults (meaning just over 80% of stations do not even have 1 rape kit), Only 17.8% of SA police stations had at least 1 rape kit for children (meaning just over 82% of stations do not even have 1 rape kit)...The whole of the Eastern Cape had only 22 rape kits for children (only 2 stations has these 22 rape kits). This means not even 1% of the stations has rape kits for children. BUT THAT WAS BACK THEN. NOW, it's now 4 months later, and some province's don't have any - like the Northern Cape, and some areas in johannesburg and cape town. There is a history of this happening going back to the early 2000s. And it's a two fold problem - one, the tender is national and often there are issues with the numbers ordered, and two, the problem is that the police have a lack of funding and often run out of funds during the year, and then have to use expired kits. We have an FCS officer in Cape Town who will tell us about why this is such a catastrophe - they will show us both buccal and rape kits. Buccal kits are used to link a potential rapist's DNA to other kits. We also have an NGO called Matla A Bana, which is headed by Monique Strydom, this organization works closely with police to address the problems within child protection - like a lack of rape kits. She alerted us to it the issue. She has a prosecutor in the cape who will assist us, and will give us information about what's happening at the courts. We also have court cases where the victims have not got justice because of this issue.

Summary:
Monique Strydom: the woman who survived being taken hostage in 2000 in the Philippines. Her NGO Matla A Bana: which means “a voice against child abuse.” It began when she was asked to chair a task team that investigated child rape in South Africa. Their aim is to address the grey areas in the child protection system in South Africa.
She says that Sexual offences kit and Buccal kit (swab in mouth kit that links DNA to different cases…) are not currently available. There’s been a long history of the tenders being cancelled for various reasons – Minister Cele has said they cancelled them because there was a problem with the bidding process, but many FCS offices around the country are out of kits. One is in CAPE TOWN. I have a cape town insider FCS officer, and I have a prosecutor – both need to be hidden but can talk about the under resourcing and appalling mismanagement. I mean they re already 50 per cent short in terms of special investigating officers, but now take away the only thing they did have which was these testing kits then they can’t so their jobs. According to the last crime stats as of sept 2018 110 rapes on average per day (over 40,000 rapes, of the more than 50,000 sexual offences reported). ( according to some…1 in 4 are reported, 14% are convicted… AFRICA CHECK)


Further information:
Insider: Johan – “James” – Seasoned commanding officers that works with rape cases. He will take a rape kits and buccal kit and show them and illustrate how the other kits they’re using don’t work. He will talk about how difficult this makes his life as an officer dealing with trying to catch the perpetrators – as they are reliant on DNA, without that, and by being already under resourced they are struggling to charge and prosecute cases.
I have a second FCS officer in joburg who is willing to speak, also hidden, she is the provincial office and can explain everything as well.
There is a lot of background from Mike Waters who travelled around the country and found this to be a problem throughout all the years.
FCS officer Cons. Tshabalala went to arrest a rape suspect monday 8 july, but as they are short staffed, he didn't have anyone with him, and subsequently was shot during the arrest by the suspect and died. 17 July the Westville rapist was sentenced - and vish naidoo from SAPS will get the video from court, because despite all the gaps in resources, the units are still successful, although, not having rape kits has made their jobs now almost impossible.

Extra Budget Items:
The case study, NGO, FCS officer, prosecutor and portfolio committee members are in cape town. My FCS officer is in joburg, and one of the case studies is also in pretoria. So we just need to figure that all out.

Script:


In South Africa, sexual offences are investigated by an elite group of dedicated police detectives known as the FCS…FCS stands for Family violence, Child Protection and Sexual Offences.
Linda: “The FCS is a specialized investigation unit with special focus on crimes against women and children.”
FCS head, Major General Bafana Linda made his name by catching Fanwell Khumalo, the child serial rapist who preyed on more than 40 girls in the early 2000s.
Linda: “Policing crimes against women and children is a difficult policing. Those are crimes within the dark alleys. Normally there's no eyewitness. Our FCS is like the FBI within this country.”
These detectives are trained to treat sexual assault victims sensitively during the reporting process, collecting evidence and testifying in court. Although this should give the victim the best chance of seeing justice done, there is a nationwide shortage of the rape kits - essential for gathering evidence.
THERE IS NO WAY TO QUANTIFY HOW MANY RAPISTS HAVE SLIPPED THROUGH THE SYSTEM BECAUSE THE DNA EVIDENCE DIDN’T HOLD UP IN COURT, A SEXUAL ASSAULT KIT LIKE THIS CAN BE THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN SOMEBODY BEING CONVICTED OR WALKING AWAY SCOTT FREE.
Thabo: There's units in the whole country that doesn't have any rape kits.
Out of fear of reprisal FCS officer - *Thabo* - is hiding his identity to expose this critical shortage. Carte Blanche confirmed his story with other FCS officers and sexual crime prosecutors.
As rape kits are in such short supply we want didn’t open one. Instead this cellphone footage shows an instruction manual illustrating the package of tools used to forensically examine a victim for traces of their attacker, including combs for hairs and fibres, and swabs for fluid.
T: We are struggling to get kits now for the past year, especially the buccal sample to compare the DNA that was found on the victim with a suspect. So with each and every suspect we use two buccal samples, one is for the comparison and the other one is for the confirmation.
Parliament declared this a crisis last year, naming the shortages of rape kits as well as buccal swab kits “crippling…” And it only got worse this year, with less than 20% of police stations having rape kits.
Andrew: “In February this year we have 80 percent of our police stations with zero rape kits, rape kits for children are non-existent in 82 percent of police stations.”
DA shadow minister for police Andrew Whitfield sits on the police’s portfolio committee.
Andrew: “It is a national crisis. We cannot allow men and women and children who are sexually abused to arrive at police stations and simply not be able to get justice served.”
IF THERE ARE NO SEXUAL ASSAULT KITS, POLICE SAY THERE ARE OTHER WAYS OF GATHERING EVIDENCE, LIKE TAKING BLOOD SAMPLES, BUT OUR SOURCES SAY THAT THERE ARE NO ALTERNATIVES FOR TAKING SEMEN
T: “We don't turn away any victim...So when kits are not available, we collect as much of the clothing and stuff, and then we send it to the forensic lab.”
C: Is that as good as taking a DNA sample?
T: “Taking a sample from the victim is more effective, than just have the fluid on the clothes. And if you don't have that DNA which makes the case very difficult in court.”
If the suspect is known, the police are required to take their DNA with a buccal swab for our DNA database.
Linda: “But, in the absence of them have got an alternative, we take the suspect to the doctor to draw blood and give us the same results as what we have from the laboratory.”
T: “You can draw blood of the suspect, but it seems that that kits are also nonexistent in the service.”
C: How important are those rape kits?
Linda: “Its critical. Everything that the doctor is observing is recorded and forms part of the evidence.”
C: How do they then proceed with gathering of evidence if a victim finds out or is told that there is no rape kit?
Linda: when one area don't have, they normally talk to each other in the area to say who's got, who's got and we borrow each other. It is true that we don't have, but it does not mean that the work won't continue.
C: How long am I waiting for you to get a kit to me?
T: Especially in the rural areas, you’ll wait five or six hours.
C: What effect does it have on the victim?
T: It causes a lot of secondary trauma for that victim. Women just want to go and wash now she has to sit there for hours in that filthy semen.
I CANT IMAGINE WHAT IT MUST BE LIKE TO BE A RAPE VICTIM WAITING FOR ONE OF THESE PACKS IN THE PERPETRATORS BLOOD, SWEAT AND SEMEN, THE SECONDARY TRAUMA – UNIMAGINABLE.
And this lack of evidence can destroy a case. Monique Strydom is the founder of NPO Matla A Bana, which addresses the grey areas in the child protection system.
M: “The problem now is the ages of the kids are becoming younger, so that kid cannot testify in court. So they really need to rely on the DNA evidence.”
Strydom witnessed the trauma of rape as one of 21 hostages taken for 127 days by a terrorist group in the Philippines in 2000.
M: So I wasn't raped. I was spared that but some of the people in our group were raped and I remember that the fear of being raped was actually bigger than the fear of being killed.
So who’s to blame for the shortage of these essential forensic tools? It boils down to the tender process.
A READ-THROUGH OF MULTIPLE MEETING MINUTES IN PARLIAMENT SHOWS THAT THE TENDERS FOR SEXUAL ASSAULT AND BUCCAL SWAB KITS HAS GONE OUT REPEATEDLY, YET THE BID ADJUDICATION COMMITTEE IS YET TO TELL ANYONE WHAT THE HOLD UP WITH AWARDING THEM IS.
DNA project founder, Vanessa Lynch helped changed the law making
it mandatory for DNA to be taken from all arrested persons, to build a forensic database for the police.
Vanessa: “When the supply chain department needs to order kits they rely on the bid adjudication committee to ensure that the bids meet the specifications which are written by the forensic science laboratory. They also rely on Treasury to provide them with the funding. They don't realize that actually the length of time that it takes for each of those different departments to do the work, has a knock on effect and by the time an order is finally placed the kits may have already run out. There's a big gap in the middle and that really is your victim isn't it.”
Andrew: “There were two unsuccessful bids at one point, as well as one bid that ultimately was found successful but couldn't be awarded the tender because they were caught up in another corruption scandal.
But no one knows why the bid adjudication committee has failed to award the tender.
Andrew: “There is a fundamental element of secrecy when it comes to the bid adjudication committees, so what we'll be calling for in Parliament going forward is those adjudication committees open to the public.”
Lynch says Parliament could declare an emergency and fast-track the supply of rape kits.
V: “Maybe Parliament needs to get involved to say you have to make a decision.”
Claire: Would it not be an optimal situation if we never ran short of the kits?
Linda: Well it is for everyone's wish that you have everything, but you must remember that the issue of procurement, it involves millions. The processes that are in place have to be followed.”
Thabo says budget allocation for the 185 FCS units nationwide is limited.
T: Every unit has a budget allocated for a financial year, 80% goes towards your vehicles. But you still need stationery and your kits, everything that your office needs to do to run smoothly.
It remains to be seen how smooth things will run after Treasury cut the police’s budget by six billion rands in July.
Andrew: “The fact that we are so under-resourced in policing the 64000 officers short of the UN standard policing ratio.”
Hunting down rapists can be dangerous work says FCS officer Philip Maluleka.
P: When we applied to be police officers we knew that, we have to run towards the danger than running away from danger.
His partner constable Dumisani Tshabalala fell victim to the police’s lack of resources in July. With no other officers available for backup, he tracked down an alleged rapist and was shot dead by the suspect.

With no other officers available for backup, he tracked down an alleged rapist and was shot dead by the suspect.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Although our FCS units have some of the most exemplary officers in the country, there is little they can do when they don't have the basics - like rape kits.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: As of February this year we were leaked the rape kit stats from the various provinces, and it's appalling. Only 19.8% of SA police stations had at least 1 rape kit for adults (meaning just over 80% of stations do not even have 1 rape kit), Only 17.8% of SA police stations had at least 1 rape kit for children (meaning just over 82% of stations do not even have 1 rape kit)...The whole of the Eastern Cape had only 22 rape kits for children (only 2 stations has these 22 rape kits). This means not even 1% of the stations has rape kits for children. BUT THAT WAS BACK THEN. NOW, it's now 4 months later, and some province's don't have any - like the Northern Cape, and some areas in johannesburg and cape town. There is a history of this happening going back to the early 2000s. And it's a two fold problem - one, the tender is national and often there are issues with the numbers ordered, and two, the problem is that the police have a lack of funding and often run out of funds during the year, and then have to use expired kits. We have an FCS officer in Cape Town who will tell us about why this is such a catastrophe - they will show us both buccal and rape kits. Buccal kits are used to link a potential rapist's DNA to other kits. We also have an NGO called Matla A Bana, which is headed by Monique Strydom, this organization works closely with police to address the problems within child protection - like a lack of rape kits. She alerted us to it the issue. She has a prosecutor in the cape who will assist us, and will give us information about what's happening at the courts. We also have court cases where the victims have not got justice because of this issue.
metadata.Summary: Monique Strydom: the woman who survived being taken hostage in 2000 in the Philippines. Her NGO Matla A Bana: which means “a voice against child abuse.” It began when she was asked to chair a task team that investigated child rape in South Africa. Their aim is to address the grey areas in the child protection system in South Africa. She says that Sexual offences kit and Buccal kit (swab in mouth kit that links DNA to different cases…) are not currently available. There’s been a long history of the tenders being cancelled for various reasons – Minister Cele has said they cancelled them because there was a problem with the bidding process, but many FCS offices around the country are out of kits. One is in CAPE TOWN. I have a cape town insider FCS officer, and I have a prosecutor – both need to be hidden but can talk about the under resourcing and appalling mismanagement. I mean they re already 50 per cent short in terms of special investigating officers, but now take away the only thing they did have which was these testing kits then they can’t so their jobs. According to the last crime stats as of sept 2018 110 rapes on average per day (over 40,000 rapes, of the more than 50,000 sexual offences reported). ( according to some…1 in 4 are reported, 14% are convicted… AFRICA CHECK)
metadata.Further information: Insider: Johan – “James” – Seasoned commanding officers that works with rape cases. He will take a rape kits and buccal kit and show them and illustrate how the other kits they’re using don’t work. He will talk about how difficult this makes his life as an officer dealing with trying to catch the perpetrators – as they are reliant on DNA, without that, and by being already under resourced they are struggling to charge and prosecute cases. I have a second FCS officer in joburg who is willing to speak, also hidden, she is the provincial office and can explain everything as well. There is a lot of background from Mike Waters who travelled around the country and found this to be a problem throughout all the years. FCS officer Cons. Tshabalala went to arrest a rape suspect monday 8 july, but as they are short staffed, he didn't have anyone with him, and subsequently was shot during the arrest by the suspect and died. 17 July the Westville rapist was sentenced - and vish naidoo from SAPS will get the video from court, because despite all the gaps in resources, the units are still successful, although, not having rape kits has made their jobs now almost impossible.
